title: Accumulating, Counting, and Building Another Collection

blocks.text: A summary retains what has already been visited

To obtain a total, initialize suma = 0 before the loop. Each visit adds its value to suma. After visiting a prefix of the collection, suma represents the total of that prefix. At the end, it represents the complete total. Zero is the appropriate initial value because no data have been added yet.
The sum goes through zero, three, nine, and eleven. The variable exists outside the body so that it keeps the work done across visits and can display the result afterward.

blocks.text: An output can be a perfectly valid number yet describe the wrong task. Always compare against a collection whose total differs from its last element; a single value cannot reveal this reinitialization.
Counting matches is not summing their values

To count how many values satisfy a condition, increment a counter by one for each match. To add the matching values, add those values themselves. These are different questions: in {2, 5, 8}, there are two even values, and their sum is ten.

blocks.question: Predict the exact output, without adding quotation marks.
blocks.explanation: There are two matches, and their values, six and four, add up to ten.

blocks.question: You must count measurements greater than five. How much do you add to the counter for each match?
blocks.explanation: The counter represents a number of matches, not their magnitude.

Reference solution and review of copying

blocks.question: Predict the exact output, without adding quotation marks.
blocks.explanation: Copying a vector creates a separate collection with copies of its elements. Modifying the copy does not change the source.

blocks.question: Why is it useful to test at least one collection containing several different values?
options: Because a test with several values proves it works for every possible vector size.
Because that test replaces the empty and single-value tests.
Because it can reveal reinitialization errors and differences between counting and adding that one value may hide.
blocks.explanation: With {2, 7, 4, 1}, the sum is 14 and the count is 4; resetting the sum on each visit would leave only 1. The case {1} does not distinguish summing from counting and does not test the preservation of previous contributions. These cases do not replace the empty and single-value tests.

blocks.text: Lab criteria: preserve the sum across visits; build another vector containing all and only the selected values in their original order; leave the source unchanged; and distinguish the result's size from the sum of its values.
